analysis.title: International Market Intelligence: Morning Briefing (October 29, 2026)
key_insights: Tech is retreating after earnings disappointments from Samsung and Google. Google's weak search and advertising sales reignited AI rivalry concerns. Two supports for Tech in the latest Flows & Liquidity work are the return of retail flows and a notable short base built in QQQ.
Oil is lower on renewed US-Iran diplomatic efforts, though headlines remain volatile.

The Fed's pause was described as unclear. Economists still expect a December hike. A change to the meeting schedule (1 non-policy-setting meeting in 2027, 2 in 2028) pushed long-end rates higher and the USD weaker.

The ECB is expected to hold today and hike in December and March, with potential for a third hike given energy pressures and growth resilience. Comms on France and fiscal concerns are in focus. JPM does not expect TPI activation or a slowing of QT.

UK Budget delivered 'do no harm'. The OBR growth forecast looks too pessimistic, which implies lower borrowing. Headroom came in at the low end of expectations at £15bn, and harder fiscal decisions (such as defence funding) were pushed to next year's Spending Review. Gilts were supported by a smaller share of long-end issuance.
UK banks outperformed on the Budget because the surcharge was lower than expected and positioning was low. Burnham ruled out an early election within 12 months despite improving Labour approval.

Europe watch list: momentum signals for 10Y OAT vs Bund are extreme and can lead to profit taking on spread stabilisation. A pause in Russian refinery attacks is lifting refinery runs, with Nov exports expected 300kdb above current levels. A weaker EUR with an elevated EUR short base supports EU earnings, since a 1% EUR/USD depreciation adds about 60bps to earnings growth.
US 3Q GDP forecast cut to 3.2% from 3.5%. The September trade deficit stayed wide on capital goods imports tied to AI capex, partly offset by rising inventory accumulation.

Euro area consumers were more resilient to the energy shock than expected. Private consumption held at a steady 0.9% annualised pace in 1H26, and a slightly lower savings rate cushioned it by less than JPM had assumed.
APAC client sentiment is more bearish than the US but less so than the EU. Many APAC clients are up double digits on the year and lack incentive to re-engage until a clear trend emerges.

Client marketing trip view on the US consumer: robust, with little evidence of the K-shaped economy or cracks the media suggests. The top 4 income quintiles hold 6%-27% more real cash than at YE2019, nearly $8T in nominal terms. Retail sales run at $723bn a month YTD2026 vs $505bn in 2019. Credit card delinquencies and charge-offs are normalising to pre-COVID trends, not deteriorating.

Corporate backdrop: SPX is near all-time highs excluding post-recession periods, with record margins. HY default rates are 2.7% vs a 3.2% long-term average, after about 20% of HY market cap was upgraded to IG in the post-COVID era.

Consumer sub-sector view: airlines, cruise and hotels show robust demand. Autos and homebuilders are rates-sensitive, so parts and suppliers may make more sense. Retailers face freight costs at 30-40% of total cost that have more than tripled YTD, plus LULU and NKE issues. Quick-service trade-down is negative for the consumer strength thesis. Staples face the most margin compression risk and are likely a source of funds.

AI credit: markets are becoming more discriminating on AI infrastructure but nothing suggests a broader funding crisis. AI infrastructure has absorbed over $500 billion of debt YTD (IG over $350b, leveraged over $60b, private credit about $100b+). Hyperscaler all-in funding costs are up about 120bps. Power availability, not financing, is seen as the primary constraint on AI buildout.

AI-related CDS spreads have widened on technical selling and bank hedging of data center lending, not deteriorating fundamentals. CDS now trades above comparable cash-bond spreads, which creates opportunities for investors willing to sell protection. CRWV is highlighted because it also has converts outstanding.

IG TMT credit: MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN spreads held up while externally financed names, especially Oracle, underperformed. ORCL and SpaceX widened on reports they seek off-balance-sheet financing. Growing debt supply may pressure spreads into 2027. Nvidia is a key transmission channel for financial stress through its GPU customer relationships including CRWV.

CRWV is seen as a financing challenge, not a solvency one. JPM credit analyst projects last-12-month EBITDA rising from about $4.4b in June 2026 to $7.3b by YE and nearly $20b by YE27, with about $130b of contracted revenue and flexibility to finance via SPVs and credit backstops.

France: contagion fears are called exaggerated. France has a roughly 3% primary deficit and debt/GDP near 120%, and the 180% threshold is 10-15 years away on unchanged policy. Italy could stabilise debt with about 50bp of spending cuts vs over 300bp for France. The ECB backstop (TPI, OMT, PEPP flexibility) limits disorderly spread widening. JPM sees a French idiosyncratic story, not a sovereign crisis 2.0.

French bonds: the move was worsened by hedge fund crowding in carry proxies and about 60% non-resident ownership. OATs discount debt/GDP above 150% and an implied deficit above 8%. JPM sees no material reversal until 2Q27 elections but room for relief into year-end around the budget discussion.

EU banks: the tape echoes the 2011-12 sovereign crisis, but JPM sees the earnings trend unchanged and says dips of more than 15% vs the index should be bought. Call ratio spreads and call spreads are favored.
French equities split into Exporters (geopolitics/tariffs driver) and Domestics (fiscal driver). Both are shorted, which makes France a funder at the country level.

Midterms: federal AI regulation is unlikely because Trump would veto and Democrats cannot reach a 2/3 majority. State-level headwinds are not uniform. A Democratic House could defund Middle East military efforts. Tariff policy is unlikely to change. Longer-dated bonds could see a bid if Democrats halt deficit spending.

Treasuries: before the Oct 22 rally the view was that a 10Y yield of 5.50% was likelier than 5.00%. The market prices a December 2026 hike and two in FY27. Clients see upside risk to that pricing. Downside risk is a near-term end to the US/Iran conflict and quick normalisation of oil and shipping costs, held with low conviction.

Trade ideas discussed split AI vs non-AI. Pushbacks on AI: semi revenue is driven by supply-constrained price spikes that are unsustainable in a DCF, neocloud turmoil may spread with bankruptcy risk, and software is no longer a funding source. Security and infra software are consensus longs. Timing to buy needs a positioning flush, hyperscaler capex confirmation, semis earnings, tighter credit and seasonality, pointing to early November.

Breadth: since the July 28 local lows SPX is +4.8% through Oct 22, but over half the index has a negative return and 69% of stocks lag the SPX. This makes single-stock longs hedged with sector ETFs difficult. The 10Y averaged 3.14% this decade through Oct 22 vs 2.39% in the 2010s.

An 'everything rally' of AI and ex-AI together is possible short term but not longer term. About 65% of SPX companies cited AI operational improvement in 2Q26 earnings but under 5% quantified it, so AI quantification may become a management quality metric.

Cyclicals: client interest is in Financials (GSIBs, credit cards) and Energy. Aerospace/defense is viewed negatively on Blue Wave risk, though a lame-duck military funding bill could surprise higher. Funding shorts for Tech could combine Consumer, Healthcare, small/mid caps and Europe.

Other assets: Dollar seen range-bound and likely at a local high. Gold is interesting after its decline but trades inversely to the Dollar. No one viewed credit as superior to equities. Copper bull case agreed. Silver is viewed as part of the AI trade.

Global equity stance: tactically bullish. Preference is long US and Asia (Japan, Korea, Taiwan) vs EU. Broadening can return, more clearly in the US than the EU, and EU conviction needs stable EGB spreads. Longs: Tech and supercycle themes, EU and JA banks, EU industrials, JA machinery, EU miners, EU pharma, UKX, selectively consumer. Shorts: AI-vulnerable ex-software, short-cycle data center capex names, EU insurance, autos, chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, MedTech, MDAX.

Emerging markets: JPM is bullish on EM, which has recovered over 9% of its drawdown since the end-July bottom. Trades: tactically long China Star 50 vs KWEB, long Korea vs Southeast Asia, long Taiwan, plus long Brazil (EWZ) and EM (EEM) as hedges.

Positioning: hedge funds are -3.3% MTD globally while SPX is +0.2% MTD, so alpha, not beta, drove the drawdown. CTAs were the most consistent sellers, with US equity exposure falling every day since 10/13, led by Nasdaq. HF selling was moderate and retail remained net buyers at the slowest pace in a year.

Sector flows: combined ETF, retail and HF 60d flows into Info Tech are near record highs (+3z). Flows into Utilities, Real Estate and Materials are at or near extreme lows. Healthcare is the defensive exception.

Stabilisation signals: crowding returns are low on a 60d basis, multi-strat de-grossing slowed, quants are re-grossing and ETFs are buying the dip. Risks: Eq L/S alpha still deteriorating, CTAs neutral and able to sell further, soft retail demand, and gross leverage still above average.

market_movers.rationale: Long Brazil suggested as a hedge on a potential structural policy shift after the second-round presidential vote, and as a diversifier against EM AI weakness and geopolitical risk.
Long EM suggested for greater exposure to potential market broadening.
China Star 50 preferred over China Internet because large-cap internet names are more exposed to the Chinese consumer.
Credit analyst sees a financing challenge, not solvency, with EBITDA projected to rise sharply and CDS trading at a slightly positive basis.

sector_views.rationale: Revenue and earnings differential point to Tech domination once markets stabilise. Key longs across inference, semi cap, less-levered hyperscalers and AI-vulnerable software.
Earnings trend unchanged, dips of more than 15% vs the index should be bought, and positioning is low.
Selectively long. Travel demand robust, rates-sensitive autos and homebuilders weak, retailers face freight costs, staples face margin compression.
Clients see a negative outlook on potential Blue Wave halting a military funding spike.
Combined flows are at or near extreme lows on 20d and 60d horizons.
Defensive exception in flows (20d +2.8z, HF-led), and suggested as a funding offset to Tech exposure.
Listed among shorts in the global equity monetization stance.

earnings_insights: Samsung and Google reported disappointing results on Oct 28-29. Google's search and advertising sales disappointed, reigniting AI rivalry concerns. No EPS or revenue figures are given.
Earnings calendar per the report: Oct 28 GOOG, MSFT, UBS, DBL, SAN, BNP, STAN. Oct 29 AMZN, INTC, EU banks (incl. GLE), Korea memory.
A 1% EUR/USD depreciation contributes about 60bps to EU earnings growth (estimate). This month's EU outperformers have a higher share of US revenue.
Clients flagged that EU bank earnings trend is unchanged despite the sovereign spread move. Recent airline, cruise and hotel earnings confirmed robust demand despite higher prices.
Semis earnings reports are listed as one of the conditions for a re-entry into AI/Tech, pointing to early November.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Forecast cut after a wide September trade deficit on AI-related capital goods, partly offset by inventory accumulation.
Consumers proved resilient to the energy shock, with a slightly lower savings rate cushioning less than assumed.

macro_indicators.reading: Hike in Dec 2026 and 2x in FY27
macro_indicators.interpretation: Clients see upside risk to this pricing. Fed dots show no hikes in FY27, cuts in FY28 and FY29, and 2% in FY29.

macro_indicators.reading: Hold today, hikes in Dec and March, possible third hike
macro_indicators.interpretation: Energy pressure and growth resilience support more tightening.
Low end of expectations, with tougher decisions deferred to the next Spending Review.
Corporate sector healthy, even as a proxy for non-public business.
Spending growth almost double the pre-COVID rate, so higher energy prices are not crowding out discretionary spend.
Pre-rally view on the 10Y yield. The 10Y has averaged 3.14% this decade through Oct 22.
Headwinds but far from the 180% threshold. OATs discount debt/GDP above 150% and a deficit above 8%.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically long China Star 50 (Science and Tech Innovation) vs short China Internet (KWEB)
trade_ideas.rationale: Captures more innovative and AI-exposed names while large-cap internet is more exposed to the Chinese consumer.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically long Korea vs South East Asia (ASEA)
trade_ideas.rationale: Expresses the AI winners vs losers view.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically long Taiwan after the Global Tech selloff in July
trade_ideas.rationale: Taiwan offers less volatile exposure to AI and Asia Tech than Korea.
Potential structural policy shift after the second-round presidential vote, diversification against EM AI weakness and relative resilience to geopolitical risk.

trade_ideas.description: Long EM (EEM) for exposure to potential broadening
trade_ideas.rationale: Continued global macro strength, AI capex tailwinds and scope for policy easing.

trade_ideas.description: EU banks call ratio spreads and call spreads, buying dips of more than 15% vs the index
trade_ideas.rationale: Earnings trend for EU banks is unchanged and the backdrop is attractive for these structures.
trade_ideas.risk: EU sovereign spread widening in the style of 2011-12.

trade_ideas.description: Sell CDS protection on AI names where CDS trades above cash bonds (positive basis), e.g. CRWV
trade_ideas.rationale: Bank hedging of data center lending is pressuring CDS spreads beyond fundamentals, and selling protection requires only initial margin.
trade_ideas.risk: Financing constraints for leveraged GPU and data center developers.

trade_ideas.description: Option hedges: keep MCX < UKX, and short France vs EU Domestics
trade_ideas.rationale: Clarity needed on spending, pragmatism and ideology for the UK, and politics and dislocation for France.

risk_factors: Eq L/S alpha is still deteriorating and CTAs could sell further if markets do not rebound.
Retail demand is soft and positioning has not fully cleared.
Growing AI debt supply could pressure credit spreads into 2027, and leveraged GPU and data center financing is vulnerable to rising rates.
Circular financing and Nvidia credit support introduce concentration and correlated downside risk.
Neocloud turmoil may spread across the group with bankruptcy risk.
Semi revenue driven by supply-constrained price spikes may be unsustainable.
EGB spread instability in France could hold back EU broadening.
Fed hikes above market pricing given strong household and corporate balance sheets, accelerating growth and inflation.
Retail margin pressure from freight costs and staples margin compression.
Aerospace/defense exposure to a Blue Wave halting military funding.

vol_and_positioning: Hedge funds are -3.3% MTD globally (from -2.1% last week) with YTD returns at +4.7% (from +6%). Eq L/S 20d alpha of -2.9% is the worst since Feb '21 and Multi-Strat alpha the worst since Aug '24. 60d crowding returns of -4.1% are back to July '24 levels.

HF net flows were -0.9z (gross -0.6z). Multi-strat 5d gross de-grossing slowed to -0.9% from -3.3%, and quants kept adding gross (80th percentile). CTA US equity exposure has fallen every day since 10/13, led by Nasdaq, and sits at about the 45th percentile long term.
Retail stayed a net buyer at the slowest 20d pace in a year (5th percentile). ETFs were buyers, led by Tech.

Combined ETF + Retail + HF 60d relative flows into Info Tech are +3z vs a +3.4z peak in late September. Utilities 60d -2.5z (lowest since Jan '24), Real Estate 20d -4.9z, Materials 60d -2.7z, Healthcare 20d +2.8z.

US TPM is at the 28th percentile, Europe the 8th, and China/HK at -2z. Eq L/S net leverage is at 12-month and 3-year lows, but gross leverage is still at the 77th percentile (12m) and 95th (5yr) after falling 4.4% WoW.
AI Core Revenue and Semis positioning fell to the 94th percentile long term from the 99th.
Notable short base built in QQQ, and an elevated EUR short base supports EU earnings.
MOMO signal for 10Y OAT vs Bund is at -2.9 z-scores, flagging profit-taking risk on spread stabilisation.
Hedges and options: call ratio spreads and call spreads on EU banks, keep MCX < UKX, short France vs EU Domestics.
geopolitical: US-Iran diplomatic efforts renewed, pushing oil lower, though headlines stay volatile.
US/Iran conflict: a near-term end would normalise oil, refined product, petrochemical and shipping/insurance costs and lower expected Fed hikes.
France fiscal concerns and the ECB's TPI/OMT backstop, with French elections in 2Q27.
UK Budget 'do no harm' and Burnham ruling out an early election within 12 months.
Pause in Russian refinery attacks is lifting refinery runs and expected Nov exports.
US midterms: AI regulation, tariff policy, and a Democratic House potentially defunding Middle East military efforts.
Brazil second-round presidential election at the end of the month.
China Central Committee plenum, Israeli elections, EU-Canada Summit in Montreal and a G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting hosted by the US Secretary of State appear on the catalyst calendar.

Economists still expect a December Fed hike.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers are fundamentally well-positioned, capital remains available, and CRWV's EBITDA is projected to rise from about $4.4b to nearly $20b by YE27 with about $130b of contracted revenue.
tension_points.bear_case: Leveraged GPU and data center developers face tighter financing, debt issuance is growing, and CDS spreads are widening on bank hedging.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler capex confirmation and credit tightening are named as conditions for re-engaging AI, so continued credit spread widening would undercut the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: Debt/GDP of c.120% is far from the 180% threshold, Italy and Spain have stronger fiscal profiles, the ECB backstop limits disorderly widening, and EU banks' earnings trend is unchanged.
tension_points.bear_case: EGB spreads wider, EUR and EU banks lower echo 2011-12, and French bonds are hurt by crowded positioning and 60% non-resident ownership.
tension_points.what_invalidates: EU banks dips of more than 15% vs the index would be a buying point and EGB spread instability would delay EU broadening.

tension_points.bull_case: Top income quintiles hold 6%-27% more real cash than at YE2019, retail sales run well above pre-COVID, and delinquencies are normalising.
tension_points.bear_case: Retail freight costs have tripled YTD, quick-service trade-down is occurring, and staples face margin compression.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong household and corporate balance sheets, accelerating growth and inflation point to more hikes than the Dec 2026 and 2x FY27 priced.
tension_points.bear_case: A near-term end to the US/Iran conflict and quick normalisation of oil and shipping costs would mean fewer hikes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A near-term end to the US/Iran conflict followed by quick normalisation of oil, refined product, petrochemical and shipping/insurance rates.
